title: Phishing to business email compromise
oneLiner: An accounts-payable specialist falls for a fake login page. The attacker wants to use her mailbox to redirect a vendor payment.
teaching: Both SOCs see the same alerts at the same moment. Everything the agentic SOC gains is on the response side.

labels.rootCause: Dana visited halvorsen-login.example (registered 3 days earlier) one minute before the suspicious sign-in
labels.attackSummary: adversary-in-the-middle phishing; Dana's session token was stolen and replayed from 203.0.113.45 (Amsterdam, NL)
labels.hotEvidence: a sign-in from a never-seen device, followed by mailbox access through the mail API
labels.ambiguousNote: The sign-in came from an in-state residential IP with MFA approved. That looks legitimate, so the analyst works through mailbox audit logs and other hot data.
labels.objectiveImpact: A fraudulent "Brightline Freight changed bank details" request went from Dana's mailbox to the AP manager. Finance now has to catch it by hand before Friday's payment run.
labels.undetected: No alert fired at any point. The fraud will most likely be noticed by finance days later, if at all.
labels.mitre: T1566.002 phishing link, T1557 adversary-in-the-middle, T1550.004 web session cookie, T1114.003 email forwarding rule
labels.lureGone: the phishing email was purged from all inboxes
labels.containDone: Dana's sessions revoked, password reset, any attacker inbox rules removed
labels.blockDone: halvorsen-login.example blocked at DNS/proxy; the lure removed from all 12 inboxes
labels.humanPivot: Pivots across the identity provider, mailbox audit, and web logs, one console at a time.
labels.playbook: SOAR revokes sessions, resets the password, and removes inbox rules.
labels.rootMissingNote: The other targets of the phishing email stay exposed.
labels.rootSearch: Dana's web activity before the suspicious sign-in
labels.fullFinding: The same email went to 12 people.
labels.fullPackage: revoke Dana's sessions and reset password; block halvorsen-login.example; purge the email from all 12 inboxes
labels.containPackage: revoke Dana's sessions, reset password, remove inbox rules
labels.blockPackage: block halvorsen-login.example; purge the email from all 12 inboxes
labels.pivotText: Same domain found in a message sent to 12 people.
labels.secondVictim: the phishing link was still live when another employee clicked it

events.title: Dana signs in from the Chicago office
events.summary: A normal start to the day.

events.title: Phishing email reaches 12 finance staff
events.summary: "Action required: vendor portal password expires today." The email gateway lets it through because the domain is too new to be on any blocklist.

email.subject: Action required: vendor portal password expires today

events.title: Dana clicks the link
events.summary: Her laptop looks up and opens halvorsen-login.example, a domain registered 3 days ago.

events.title: Attacker steals Dana's session
events.summary: Dana enters her password and approves the MFA push on the fake page. The page relays both to the real sign-in, and the attacker keeps the session token. The identity provider sees the sign-in from 203.0.113.45 (Amsterdam, NL).

events.title: Attacker starts reading Dana's mailbox
events.summary: Replays the stolen token and reads mail through the mail API.

events.title: Attacker hides a forwarding rule
events.summary: Mail containing "invoice", "payment", or "remittance" is forwarded to an outside address, marked read, and moved to a folder Dana never opens.

events.title: Priya clicks the same link
events.summary: Priya gets suspicious at the password page and closes it. No credentials lost.

events.title: Attacker finds a vendor invoice thread
events.summary: Searches the mailbox and finds Brightline Freight's invoices ahead of Friday's payment run.

events.title: Fraudulent bank-change request sent
events.summary: From Dana's real mailbox to her manager: "Brightline Freight has new bank details, please update before Friday."

email.subject: RE: Brightline Freight — updated remittance details

events.title: Sam opens the email after lunch and signs in
events.summary: The link still works, so Sam's session is stolen too.

rules.name: Impossible travel
rules.logic: Two sign-ins for the same user that would need travel faster than 900 km/h.
rules.triageNote: The IP belongs to a hosting provider in Amsterdam, not the corporate VPN.
rules.agentTriageNote: Hosting-provider IP, never-seen device, MFA approved from an unusual location: likely session theft. Investigating.

rules.name: Newly registered domain, then a sign-in
rules.logic: A visit to a domain under 7 days old, followed by a sign-in by the same user within 5 minutes.
rules.triageNote: The alert already names the phishing domain. Classic adversary-in-the-middle pattern.
rules.agentTriageNote: A 3-day-old domain, then a sign-in from a new device a minute later: adversary-in-the-middle phishing. Investigating.

rules.name: External forwarding rule created
rules.logic: A new inbox rule that forwards mail to an outside address.
rules.triageNote: An accounts-payable user forwarding payment emails outside the company. Worth a closer look.
rules.agentTriageNote: External forwarding of finance keywords, on an accounts-payable user, 35 minutes after a sign-in from a never-seen device. High risk despite the medium severity. Investigating.

notes.enriched: The domain age and the lookalike match are what make this one event stand out from the millions of normal lookups that day.
